newsitem.title: UK: Lloyds Abbey Life full year tops forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Lloyds Abbey Life full year tops forecasts.

text.p: Lloyds TSB insurance subsidiary Lloyds Abbey Life reported a 30 percent increase in profits on Wednesday and said performance across all its divisions had improved.
Pre-tax profits for the 12 months to December 31 were ahead of analyst expectations at 548.1 million stg, up from 421.5 million stg last year.
The results will be the last separate declaration of results after the company became a wholly-owned subsidiary of Lloyds TSB at the end of 1996.
Lloyds Abbey Life chief executive Stephen Maran said the rise in profits reflected a continuing focus on customer needs and increased operational efficiencies.
Industry analysts expect further cost savings to come through from the integration with Lloyds TSB.
Life assurance profits in the year rose by 23 percent to 327.3 million stg and sales of life, pensions and unit trusts increased 16 percent.

"I don't think it tells us anything we didn't know but it provides a fairly positive picture of financial services all round. Prospects for 1997 and 1998 look fairly attractive," said one industry analyst.
Annual premium business rose five percent to 127.4 million stg and single premium products were six percent higher at 703.9 million stg.
Sales of PEPs and unit trusts showed a healthy 56 percent rise to 504.6 million stg.
Analysts said the figures included an unexpected 13.7 million stg provision for pension misselling and a gain from a change in taxation treatment.
"The figures are undoubtedly good. Abbey Life results were in-line and BlackHorse Financial Services and Lloyds Bowmaker a bit better," said the analyst.
"The eye-catcher was Lloyds Bank Insurance Services which had a big jump in profits and the 13 million pound (stg) turnaround in the estate agency was very welcome."
The company said it would be best placed to meet the challenges of an increasingly competitive market as a full member of Lloyds TSB.
The high street banking group which already held a 62.6 percent stake in Lloyds Abbey Life completed the acquisition of the outstanding stake in December 1996.
